title: Jack Carey's band, the Robichaux clarinettist and not reading music
summary: Members of Carey's band, a clarinettist nicknamed Robichaux, a Birmingham offer, and playing by ear at a tea room.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I believe. Well who was with Jack Carey in there? Jack Carey, myself, George Foster, Little Chinese, George Boyd. Well I'll tell you about that now. They had a boy, I don't know if he's Kent the Old Man Robichaux or not, but we used to call him Robichaux and he claimed he's a relation to Old Man Robichaux, he played violin at the Larry Theater. He's real light with nice hair. Well he played clarinet with us at the Moes. Played what?

Robichaux, well anybody around here tell him, he's younger than any of us too. But I do believe he did. We all called him Robichaux, see because I went to his house one time to get him to play. And he said that we should whistle for musicians, like that. So his old mother, somebody come to the door and said, what dog are you calling? I said Robichaux. Boy I point up, I said Robichaux. So he come to the door and say old man, I said yeah I am, I said I'm feeling no mind. So you know it's one of them things you know. And Lorenzo Stahl, I'm just putting some stuff in now, Lorenzo Stahl, he was with Jack Carey, he was playing manager. So some man wanted us to go to Birmingham to play two nights, pay all the expenses and give us a hundred dollars a man a night. So Lorenzo was so funny you know. He asked Jack, he said, Jack how much you going to give him, talking about Robichaux. Jack said I'm going to give him two hundred dollars. He said man give me some of that money. I said boy all that money, boy sitting up there playing I Will Follow Where They Lead It. So you know I don't want to like that.
Boy he made Robichaux for a boy cry like a baby. That's true for me to God ever. Did you read with those bands like Ernest Johnson? No. Did you read with Jack Carey?

No. Uh uh. I ain't going to lie. Yeah, well nobody was, well that's good. Tell you about one thing happened. A white lady right down the bottom of the tea room, what's the name of that room, it was up your town here. Yeah. She had a piano copy of her song. It's the truth. And she brought that piano copy and asked us what we played and I played it down. I'll tell you what it was. That piece that I'll never get along as I left. And they couldn't follow me but you know the bass and the guitar that's hitting along with me and she thought it was mighty wonderful. She said I think that's nice. But the other boy just now they couldn't play.
